    Data

    Supervised datasets stored as shapes, including tables and image samples.

    DataShape #

    Bases: Shape, ABC

    One supervised dataset: inputs, optional outputs, and a train or test split.

    portion keeps a shuffled subset of the rows as the working set. The rows that were left out are the validation set. Pass materialize_validation_from_portion=False to store only their indices until materialize_validation_from_portion() copies the arrays.

    Attributes:

    Name Type Description
    inputs

    Working input rows, after portion is applied.
    outputs

    Working output rows, or None for input-only data.
    indices

    Sorted positions of the working rows in the original array.
    num_data

    Number of working rows.
    file_indices Array | Sequence[str] | None

    File name or id for each working row, when the data came from files.
    been_split bool

    True after test_train_split() has stored train and test rows.
    train_indices Array

    Positions of the training rows inside inputs.
    train_inputs Array

    Training inputs.
    train_outputs Array | None

    Training outputs, or None when this shape has no outputs.
    test_indices Array

    Positions of the test rows inside inputs.
    test_inputs Array

    Test inputs.
    test_outputs Array | None

    Test outputs, or None when this shape has no outputs.
    validation_inputs Array | None

    Held-out inputs, once they have been copied out.
    validation_outputs Array | None

    Held-out outputs, once they have been copied out.
    validation_indices Array | None

    Held-out positions, while the copy is still deferred.

    class DataShape(Shape, ABC):
    """One supervised dataset: inputs, optional outputs, and a train or test split.

    ``portion`` keeps a shuffled subset of the rows as the working set. The rows
    that were left out are the validation set. Pass
    ``materialize_validation_from_portion=False`` to store only their indices until
    ``materialize_validation_from_portion()`` copies the arrays.

    Attributes:
        inputs: Working input rows, after ``portion`` is applied.
        outputs: Working output rows, or ``None`` for input-only data.
        indices: Sorted positions of the working rows in the original array.
        num_data: Number of working rows.
        file_indices: File name or id for each working row, when the data came from files.
        been_split: True after ``test_train_split()`` has stored train and test rows.
        train_indices: Positions of the training rows inside ``inputs``.
        train_inputs: Training inputs.
        train_outputs: Training outputs, or ``None`` when this shape has no outputs.
        test_indices: Positions of the test rows inside ``inputs``.
        test_inputs: Test inputs.
        test_outputs: Test outputs, or ``None`` when this shape has no outputs.
        validation_inputs: Held-out inputs, once they have been copied out.
        validation_outputs: Held-out outputs, once they have been copied out.
        validation_indices: Held-out positions, while the copy is still deferred.

    """

    been_split: bool = False

    train_indices: Array
    train_inputs: Array
    train_outputs: Array | None

    test_indices: Array
    test_inputs: Array
    test_outputs: Array | None

    _shape: dict[str, tuple[int, ...] | None] | None = None

    validation_inputs: Array | None = None
    validation_outputs: Array | None = None

    validation_indices: Array | None = None
    _full_inputs: Array | None = None
    _full_outputs: Array | None = None

    file_indices: Array | Sequence[str] | None = None

    def __init__(
        self,
        inputs: Array,
        outputs: Array | None = None,
        *,
        indices: Array | Sequence[int] | None = None,
        file_indices: Array | Sequence[str] | None = None,
        portion: float = 1.0,
        materialize_validation_from_portion: bool = True,
    ) -> None:
        """Keep a shuffled portion of the rows as the working set.

        ``indices`` selects those rows directly and ``portion`` is then ignored.
        Omitted indices are drawn with ``index_shuffle`` and ``portion``. The selected
        rows are stored on ``inputs`` and ``outputs``. The complement is the validation
        set. With ``materialize_validation_from_portion`` true, those rows are copied
        immediately. Otherwise, only their positions are kept, together with the full
        arrays, until ``materialize_validation_from_portion()``.

        Args:
            inputs: One row or sample per leading axis.
            outputs: Targets aligned with ``inputs``. Omit them for input-only data.
            indices: Positions to keep. Default: a shuffled fraction of the rows.
            file_indices: Label for each selected file. Stored as given.
            portion: Fraction of rows to keep when ``indices`` is omitted. Default: ``1``,
                which holds nothing out.
            materialize_validation_from_portion: Copy held-out rows during construction.
                Default: ``True``.

        Raises:
            ValueError: If ``inputs`` and ``outputs`` do not have the same number of rows.
            TypeError: If ``indices`` is not an array or a sequence.

        """
        super().__init__()

        inputs = jnp.asarray(inputs, dtype=config.get_dtype())
        if outputs is not None:
            outputs = jnp.asarray(outputs, dtype=config.get_dtype())
            if len(inputs) != len(outputs):
                msg = (
                    f"Length of Inputs: {len(inputs)} and "
                    f"Length of Outputs: {len(outputs)} must be equal."
                )
                config.LOGGER.error(msg)
                raise ValueError(msg)

        if indices is None:
            indices = jnp.asarray(
                index_shuffle(len(inputs), portion=portion),
                dtype=int,
            )
        elif not isinstance(indices, Array):
            if not isinstance(indices, Sequence):
                msg = f"'indices' must be a Sequence. Got {type(indices).__name__}"
                config.LOGGER.error(msg)
                raise TypeError(msg)
            indices = jnp.asarray(indices, dtype=int)

        indices = jnp.sort(indices)

        n_full = int(inputs.shape[0])

        used = jnp.zeros(n_full, dtype=bool)
        used = used.at[indices].set(True)
        validation_indices = jnp.sort(jnp.where(~used)[0])

        config.LOGGER.debug(f"{indices=}")

        self.validation_inputs = None
        self.validation_outputs = None
        self.validation_indices = None
        self._full_inputs = None
        self._full_outputs = None

        if validation_indices.size > 0:
            if materialize_validation_from_portion:
                self.validation_inputs = inputs[validation_indices]
                if outputs is not None:
                    self.validation_outputs = outputs[validation_indices]
            else:
                self.validation_indices = validation_indices
                self._full_inputs = inputs
                self._full_outputs = outputs

        self.inputs = inputs[indices]
        self.outputs = outputs[indices] if outputs is not None else None
        self.indices = indices
        self.file_indices = file_indices
        self.num_data = len(self.inputs)

    def materialize_validation_from_portion(self) -> None:
        """Copy deferred held-out rows into ``validation_inputs`` / ``validation_outputs``.

        Only applies when the shape was built with ``portion < 1.0`` and
        ``materialize_validation_from_portion=False``, so row indices were set aside
        at construction. Calling this again after validation is already filled is a
        no-op. If no rows were ever held out (e.g. ``portion=1.0``), there is nothing
        to copy; logs a warning and returns.
        """
        if self.validation_inputs is not None:
            return
        if self.validation_indices is None or self.validation_indices.size == 0:
            config.LOGGER.warning(
                "All DATA was used in training/testing. Use a portion less than 1.0.",
            )
            return
        assert self._full_inputs is not None
        self.validation_inputs = self._full_inputs[self.validation_indices]
        if self._full_outputs is not None:
            self.validation_outputs = self._full_outputs[self.validation_indices]
        self.validation_indices = None
        self._full_inputs = None
        self._full_outputs = None

    def clone(self, *, copy_split: bool = True) -> DataShape:
        """Return a new data shape that holds the same working rows.

        The clone is built from these rows with a fresh index range, so the original
        ``indices`` are not applied again. Validation rows are copied across. The train
        and test split is copied only when this shape has been split and ``copy_split``
        is true.

        Args:
            copy_split: Copy ``train_*``, ``test_*``, ``samples``, and ``n_points``.
                Default: ``True``.

        Returns:
            The new data shape.

        """
        config.LOGGER.debug("Cloned.")
        # Pass identity indices so `inputs`/`outputs` are already the working rows
        # (global `self.indices` are not valid row picks into the subset tensor).
        n = len(self.inputs)
        ds = DataShape(
            self.inputs,
            self.outputs,
            indices=jnp.arange(n, dtype=int),
            portion=1.0,
            materialize_validation_from_portion=True,
        )
        ds.validation_inputs = self.validation_inputs
        ds.validation_outputs = self.validation_outputs
        if self.validation_indices is not None:
            ds.validation_indices = self.validation_indices
            ds._full_inputs = self._full_inputs
            ds._full_outputs = self._full_outputs
        if copy_split and self.been_split:
            ds.train_indices = self.train_indices
            ds.test_indices = self.test_indices
            ds.train_inputs = self.train_inputs
            ds.test_inputs = self.test_inputs
            ds.train_outputs = self.train_outputs
            ds.test_outputs = self.test_outputs
            ds.samples = self.samples
            ds.n_points = self.n_points
            ds.been_split = True
        return ds

    @classmethod
    def from_files(
        cls,
        path: Path | str,
        *,
        portion: float = 1.0,
        input_folder_name: str = "input",
        output_folder_name: str | None = "output",
        mat_key: str = "groundTruth",
        resort: bool = False,
    ) -> DataShape:
        """Build a data shape from paired files in two folders.

        ``path / input_folder_name`` must be a directory. ``path / output_folder_name``
        is required unless ``output_folder_name`` is ``None``, which loads inputs only.
        Files are paired in sorted order. A numeric file stem sorts before a
        non-numeric one. Accepted suffixes are ``.jpg``, ``.png``, ``.csv``, ``.mat``,
        and ``.npy``. A MATLAB file is read from ``mat[mat_key].Segmentation``.
        ``resort`` stores an image as channels-first.

        ``portion`` selects the files. The constructor then receives that subset with
        ``portion=1``, so the file sample is not drawn a second time.

        Args:
            path: Directory that contains the input folder and the optional output folder.
            portion: Fraction of file pairs to keep. Default: ``1``.
            input_folder_name: Name of the input folder. Default: ``"input"``.
            output_folder_name: Name of the output folder, or ``None`` for inputs only.
                Default: ``"output"``.
            mat_key: MATLAB struct name. Default: ``"groundTruth"``.
            resort: Store images as channels-first. Default: ``False``.

        Returns:
            A data shape whose rows are the selected files.

        Raises:
            NotADirectoryError: If an expected folder is missing.
            ValueError: If the two folders do not contain the same number of files, or a
                MATLAB file is missing ``mat_key``.
            TypeError: If a file suffix is not supported.

        """
        input_files, output_files, indices, file_indices = _load_data_files(
            path,
            input_folder_name=input_folder_name,
            output_folder_name=output_folder_name,
            portion=portion,
        )
        inputs, outputs = _files_to_jax_arrays(
            input_files,
            output_files,
            mat_key=mat_key,
            resort=resort,
        )

        # portion = 1.0 because it would've already been split.
        return cls(
            inputs,
            outputs,
            portion=1.0,
            indices=indices,
            file_indices=file_indices,
        )

    @classmethod
    def from_table(
        cls,
        table: str | Path | pl.DataFrame,
        *,
        input_columns: str | int | Sequence[str] | Sequence[int],
        output_columns: str | int | Sequence[str] | Sequence[int] | None = None,
        portion: float = 1.0,
        drop_nulls: bool = True,
        materialize_validation_from_portion: bool = True,
    ) -> DataShape:
        """Build a data shape from a CSV file or a Polars frame.

        A column specification is one name, one index, or a sequence of one of those.
        Names and indices cannot be mixed. Output columns are optional. A one-column
        output is reshaped to ``(n, 1)``. Rows with nulls in the selected columns are
        dropped when ``drop_nulls`` is true.

        ``portion`` selects the rows before construction. The constructor then receives
        that subset with ``portion=1``.

        Args:
            table: CSV path or an existing frame. A path must end in ``.csv``.
            input_columns: Columns used as inputs.
            output_columns: Columns used as outputs. Default: no outputs.
            portion: Fraction of rows to keep. Default: ``1``.
            drop_nulls: Drop rows with a null in a selected column. Default: ``True``.
            materialize_validation_from_portion: Copy held-out rows during construction.
                Default: ``True``.

        Returns:
            A data shape with one row per table record.

        Raises:
            ValueError: If the path is not a CSV, a column list is empty, a name is
                missing, or an input column is also an output column.
            TypeError: If a specification mixes names and indices.
            IndexError: If a column index is outside the frame.

        """

        def _normalize_columns(
            spec: str | int | Sequence[str] | Sequence[int],
            available: Sequence[str],
            *,
            arg_name: str,
        ) -> list[str]:
            cols = list(available)

            if isinstance(spec, (str, int)):
                items = [spec]
            elif isinstance(spec, Sequence):
                if len(spec) == 0:
                    raise ValueError(f"'{arg_name}' cannot be empty.")
                items = list(spec)
            else:
                raise TypeError(f"'{arg_name}' has invalid type: {type(spec).__name__}")

            has_str = any(isinstance(_x, str) for _x in items)
            has_int = any(isinstance(_x, int) for _x in items)
            if has_str and has_int:
                raise TypeError(f"'{arg_name}' cannot mix str and int in one sequence.")

            if has_str:
                out = [str(_x) for _x in items]
                missing = [c for c in out if c not in cols]
                if missing:
                    raise ValueError(f"'{arg_name}' unknown columns: {missing}")
                return out

            out: list[str] = []
            for idx in items:
                if not isinstance(idx, int):
                    raise TypeError(f"'{arg_name}' must contain only str or only int.")
                if idx < 0 or idx >= len(cols):
                    raise IndexError(
                        f"'{arg_name}' index {idx} out of range [0, {len(cols) - 1}]",
                    )
                out.append(cols[idx])
            return out

        if isinstance(table, pl.DataFrame):
            df = table
        else:
            path = Path(table)
            if path.suffix.lower() != ".csv":
                raise ValueError(f"Expected .csv, got {path.suffix}")
            df = pl.read_csv(path)

        in_cols = _normalize_columns(
            input_columns,
            df.columns,
            arg_name="input_columns",
        )
        out_cols = (
            _normalize_columns(output_columns, df.columns, arg_name="output_columns")
            if output_columns is not None
            else []
        )

        overlap = sorted(set(in_cols).intersection(out_cols))
        if overlap:
            raise ValueError(f"Input/output columns overlap: {overlap}")

        selected = in_cols + out_cols
        df = df.select(selected)
        if drop_nulls:
            df = df.drop_nulls(subset=selected)

        x = df.select(in_cols).to_numpy().astype(float)
        y = None
        if out_cols:
            y = df.select(out_cols).to_numpy().astype(float)
            if y.ndim == 1:
                y = y[:, None]

        indices = None
        if portion != 1.0:
            indices = jnp.asarray(
                index_shuffle(len(x), portion=portion),
                dtype=int,
            )

        return cls(
            jnp.asarray(x, dtype=config.get_dtype()),
            (jnp.asarray(y, dtype=config.get_dtype()) if y is not None else None),
            indices=indices,
            portion=1.0,
            materialize_validation_from_portion=materialize_validation_from_portion,
        )

    @property
    def shape(self) -> dict[str, tuple[int, ...] | None]:
        """Return the input and output shapes, excluding the batch axis.

        The dictionary is cached on first use. ``output`` is ``None`` when this shape
        has no targets.

        Returns:
            A dictionary with ``input`` and ``output`` keys.

        Raises:
            RuntimeError: If ``inputs`` has not been set.

        """
        if self._shape is None:
            self._shape = self._compute_shape()
        return self._shape

    def _compute_shape(self) -> dict[str, tuple[int, ...] | None]:
        return {
            "input": self._compute_input_shape(),
            "output": self._compute_output_shape(),
        }

    def _compute_input_shape(self) -> tuple[int, ...]:
        if self.inputs is None:
            raise RuntimeError("inputs not set")
        return tuple(self.inputs.shape[1:])

    def _compute_output_shape(self) -> tuple[int, ...] | None:
        if self.outputs is None:
            return None
        return tuple(self.outputs.shape[1:])

    def _stratify_sort_indices(
        self,
        stratify_on: Literal["outputs", "inputs"],
        output_column: int,
    ) -> list[int]:
        """Return row indices sorted by the stratification column."""
        if stratify_on == "outputs":
            if self.outputs is None:
                msg = "Cannot stratify on outputs because this DataShape has no output data."
                config.LOGGER.error(msg)
                raise ValueError(msg)
            y = jnp.asarray(self.outputs)
            if y.ndim == 1:
                key = y
            elif y.ndim == 2:
                if output_column < 0 or output_column >= y.shape[1]:
                    msg = (
                        f"'output_column' out of range for outputs shape {y.shape}. "
                        f"Got {output_column}."
                    )
                    config.LOGGER.error(msg)
                    raise ValueError(msg)
                key = y[:, output_column]
            else:
                msg = (
                    f"Unsupported outputs ndim={y.ndim} for stratification. "
                    "Expected 1D or 2D outputs."
                )
                config.LOGGER.error(msg)
                raise ValueError(msg)
        else:
            x = jnp.asarray(self.inputs)
            if x.ndim != 2:
                msg = (
                    f"Unsupported inputs ndim={x.ndim} for stratification on inputs. "
                    "Expected 2D inputs."
                )
                config.LOGGER.error(msg)
                raise ValueError(msg)
            if output_column < 0 or output_column >= x.shape[1]:
                msg = (
                    f"'output_column' out of range for inputs shape {x.shape}. Got {output_column}."
                )
                config.LOGGER.error(msg)
                raise ValueError(msg)
            key = x[:, output_column]
        return list(map(int, jnp.argsort(key).tolist()))

    def test_train_split(
        self,
        split_percentage: float = 0.5,
        *,
        overwrite: bool = False,
        seed: int | None = None,  # default: config.get_seed() # 100
        mode: Literal["shuffle", "stratified", "stratified_kfold"] = "shuffle",
        stratified_assignment: Literal["random", "ordered"] = "random",
        consecutive_samples: int = 5,  # group size
        train_per_group: int | None = 3,
        # if None: derived from split_percentage
        stratify_on: Literal["outputs", "inputs"] = "outputs",
        output_column: int = 0,  # if outputs is (N, k), which column to sort by.
        # stratified_kfold: requires consecutive_samples == n_folds; in each full block,
        # position j (0..n_folds-1) is test for fold j; partial tail block -> train only
        n_folds: int = 5,
        fold: int = 0,
    ) -> None:
        """Split the working rows into train and test sets.

        A second call leaves the existing split in place and logs a warning.
        ``overwrite`` replaces it.

        ``"shuffle"`` draws a permutation and gives the first fraction to train. At
        least one row is kept for train. ``"stratified"`` sorts by one column, cuts
        that order into blocks of ``consecutive_samples``, and takes
        ``train_per_group`` rows from each block. ``None`` derives that count from
        ``split_percentage``. ``"random"`` shuffles inside the block. ``"ordered"``
        keeps the sorted order. A leftover block of one row goes to train.

        ``"stratified_kfold"`` uses the same sorted blocks. ``consecutive_samples``
        must equal ``n_folds``. Position ``fold`` in each full block is the test row,
        and the other positions are train. A short tail block goes to train.
        ``split_percentage`` is not used in this mode.

        ``samples`` and ``n_points`` are set from the training inputs.

        Args:
            split_percentage: Fraction of rows for training. Required in ``(0, 1)`` for
                ``"shuffle"`` and ``"stratified"``. Default: ``0.5``.
            overwrite: Replace an existing split. Default: ``False``.
            seed: Seed for the shuffle. ``None`` uses ``config.get_seed()``.
            mode: ``"shuffle"``, ``"stratified"``, or ``"stratified_kfold"``.
                Default: ``"shuffle"``.
            stratified_assignment: ``"random"`` or ``"ordered"`` inside each stratified
                block. Default: ``"random"``.
            consecutive_samples: Block length for the stratified modes. Default: ``5``.
            train_per_group: Training rows taken from each stratified block. ``None``
                uses ``split_percentage``. Default: ``3``.
            stratify_on: ``"outputs"`` or ``"inputs"``. Default: ``"outputs"``.
            output_column: Column used as the sort key. Default: ``0``.
            n_folds: Number of folds for ``"stratified_kfold"``. Default: ``5``.
            fold: Which position in each block is the test row. Default: ``0``.

        Raises:
            ValueError: If the fraction, mode, block size, fold, or sort column is not valid.

        """
        if self.been_split is not True or overwrite is True:
            if overwrite:
                msg = "This DataShape was previously split. Overwriting."
                config.LOGGER.warning(msg)
            if split_percentage <= 0 or (split_percentage >= 1 and mode != "stratified_kfold"):
                msg = (
                    "`split_percentage` must be between 0 and 1 (non-exclusive)."
                    f" Got {split_percentage}."
                )
                config.LOGGER.error(msg)
                raise ValueError(msg)

            if seed is None:
                seed = config.get_seed()

            if mode == "shuffle":
                indices = index_shuffle(self.num_data, seed=seed)
                split = max(int(self.num_data * split_percentage), 1)
                self.train_indices = jnp.asarray(sorted(indices[:split]), dtype=int)
                self.test_indices = jnp.asarray(sorted(indices[split:]), dtype=int)
            elif mode == "stratified_kfold":
                if n_folds < 2:
                    msg = "'n_folds' must be >= 2 for stratified_kfold mode."
                    config.LOGGER.error(msg)
                    raise ValueError(msg)
                if fold < 0 or fold >= n_folds:
                    msg = f"'fold' must be in [0, n_folds). Got fold={fold}, n_folds={n_folds}."
                    config.LOGGER.error(msg)
                    raise ValueError(msg)
                if consecutive_samples < 2:
                    msg = "'consecutive_samples' must be >= 2 for stratified_kfold mode."
                    config.LOGGER.error(msg)
                    raise ValueError(msg)
                if consecutive_samples != n_folds:
                    msg = (
                        "'stratified_kfold' requires `consecutive_samples` == `n_folds` "
                        "so each ascending-life block assigns one sample per fold."
                    )
                    config.LOGGER.error(msg)
                    raise ValueError(msg)
                sorted_idx = self._stratify_sort_indices(stratify_on, output_column)
                train_idx: list[int] = []
                test_idx: list[int] = []
                for start in range(0, len(sorted_idx), consecutive_samples):
                    block = sorted_idx[start : start + consecutive_samples]
                    if len(block) < consecutive_samples:
                        train_idx.extend(block)
                        continue
                    for j, idx in enumerate(block):
                        if j == fold:
                            test_idx.append(idx)
                        else:
                            train_idx.append(idx)
                self.train_indices = jnp.asarray(sorted(train_idx), dtype=int)
                self.test_indices = jnp.asarray(sorted(test_idx), dtype=int)
            elif mode == "stratified":
                if stratified_assignment not in ("random", "ordered"):
                    msg = (
                        "`stratified_assignment` must be 'random' or 'ordered'. "
                        f"Got {stratified_assignment!r}."
                    )
                    config.LOGGER.error(msg)
                    raise ValueError(msg)
                if consecutive_samples < 2:
                    msg = "`consecutive_samples` must be >= 2 for stratified mode."
                    config.LOGGER.error(msg)
                    raise ValueError(msg)
                sorted_idx = self._stratify_sort_indices(stratify_on, output_column)
                if train_per_group is None:
                    tpg: int = round(consecutive_samples * split_percentage)
                else:
                    tpg = int(train_per_group)
                tpg = max(1, min(tpg, consecutive_samples - 1))
                train_idx = []
                test_idx = []
                for start in range(0, len(sorted_idx), consecutive_samples):
                    block = sorted_idx[start : start + consecutive_samples]
                    if len(block) == 1:
                        train_idx.extend(block)
                        continue
                    if stratified_assignment == "random":
                        random.Random(seed).shuffle(block)
                    k = min(max(1, tpg), len(block) - 1)
                    train_idx.extend(block[:k])
                    test_idx.extend(block[k:])
                self.train_indices = jnp.asarray(sorted(train_idx), dtype=int)
                self.test_indices = jnp.asarray(sorted(test_idx), dtype=int)
            else:
                msg = (
                    f"Invalid split mode: {mode}. "
                    "Use 'shuffle', 'stratified', or 'stratified_kfold'."
                )
                config.LOGGER.error(msg)
                raise ValueError(msg)
            self.train_inputs, self.test_inputs = (
                self.inputs[self.train_indices],
                self.inputs[self.test_indices],
            )
            if self.outputs is None:
                self.train_outputs = None
                self.test_outputs = None
            else:
                self.train_outputs, self.test_outputs = (
                    self.outputs[self.train_indices],
                    self.outputs[self.test_indices],
                )
            self.samples = self.train_inputs
            self.n_points = len(self.train_inputs)
            self.been_split = True
        else:
            msg = (
                "This DataShape has already been split into test/train. "
                "Continuing without making changes"
            )
            config.LOGGER.warning(msg)

    def draw(
        self,
        data_index: int = 0,
        *,
        show_normals: bool = False,
        normal_scale: float = 1.0,
        fig: Figure | None = None,
        ax: Axes | None = None,
        fig_size: tuple[float, float] | None = None,
        show: bool = True,
        input_channel: DrawChannel = 0,
        output_channel: DrawChannel = 0,
        cmap: str = "grey",
        subplot_orientation: SubPlotOrientation = "horizontal",
        show_title: bool = False,
        show_captions: bool = True,
        save: bool = False,
        save_location: str | Path | None = None,
        save_name: str | None = "comparison.pdf",
        resort: bool | None = None,
    ) -> tuple[Figure, Axes]:
        """Plot one sample and, when outputs exist, the matching target.

        ``show_normals``, ``normal_scale``, ``fig``, ``ax``, and ``fig_size`` are
        accepted so this method can stand in for [`Shape.draw`][pinnjax.geometry.base.Shape.draw].
        The image plot builds its own figure and does not use them.

        ``input_channel`` and ``output_channel`` choose one leading channel, ``"rgb"``,
        or ``"all"``. ``"all"`` draws one panel per channel. ``None`` uses the array as
        stored. Panels are laid out in one row or one column.

        Args:
            data_index: Sample to draw. Default: ``0``.
            show_normals: Ignored. Default: ``False``.
            normal_scale: Ignored. Default: ``1``.
            fig: Ignored. Default: ``None``.
            ax: Ignored. Default: ``None``.
            fig_size: Ignored.
            show: Display the figure before returning it. Default: ``True``.
            input_channel: Channel of the input sample. Default: ``0``.
            output_channel: Channel of the output sample. Default: ``0``.
            cmap: Colormap for a single-channel image. Default: ``"grey"``.
            subplot_orientation: ``"horizontal"`` or ``"vertical"``. Default: ``"horizontal"``.
            show_title: Put the sample index and file name above the figure.
                Default: ``False``.
            show_captions: Title each panel. Default: ``True``.
            save: Write the figure to disk. Default: ``False``.
            save_location: Directory for the saved figure. Default: ``None``.
            save_name: File name. Default: ``"comparison.pdf"``.
            resort: Move channel axes before display. ``None`` moves a single leading
                channel only. Default: ``None``.

        Returns:
            The Matplotlib figure and its first axes.

        Raises:
            IndexError: If ``data_index`` is outside the working rows.
            ValueError: If a channel setting does not match the array shape.

        """
        del show_normals, normal_scale, fig, ax, fig_size
        if data_index < 0 or data_index >= len(self.inputs):
            raise IndexError(
                f"Index {data_index} out of range for dataset length {len(self.inputs)}",
            )
        return _draw_arrays(
            self.inputs,
            self.outputs,
            data_index=data_index,
            input_channel=input_channel,
            output_channel=output_channel,
            cmap=cmap,
            file_indices=self.file_indices,
            subplot_orientation=subplot_orientation,
            show_title=show_title,
            show_captions=show_captions,
            show=show,
            save=save,
            save_location=save_location,
            save_name=save_name,
            resort=resort,
        )

    def __init__(
    self,
    inputs: Array,
    outputs: Array | None = None,
    *,
    indices: Array | Sequence[int] | None = None,
    file_indices: Array | Sequence[str] | None = None,
    portion: float = 1.0,
    materialize_validation_from_portion: bool = True,
) -> None:
    """Keep a shuffled portion of the rows as the working set.

    ``indices`` selects those rows directly and ``portion`` is then ignored.
    Omitted indices are drawn with ``index_shuffle`` and ``portion``. The selected
    rows are stored on ``inputs`` and ``outputs``. The complement is the validation
    set. With ``materialize_validation_from_portion`` true, those rows are copied
    immediately. Otherwise, only their positions are kept, together with the full
    arrays, until ``materialize_validation_from_portion()``.

    Args:
        inputs: One row or sample per leading axis.
        outputs: Targets aligned with ``inputs``. Omit them for input-only data.
        indices: Positions to keep. Default: a shuffled fraction of the rows.
        file_indices: Label for each selected file. Stored as given.
        portion: Fraction of rows to keep when ``indices`` is omitted. Default: ``1``,
            which holds nothing out.
        materialize_validation_from_portion: Copy held-out rows during construction.
            Default: ``True``.

    Raises:
        ValueError: If ``inputs`` and ``outputs`` do not have the same number of rows.
        TypeError: If ``indices`` is not an array or a sequence.

    """
    super().__init__()

    inputs = jnp.asarray(inputs, dtype=config.get_dtype())
    if outputs is not None:
        outputs = jnp.asarray(outputs, dtype=config.get_dtype())
        if len(inputs) != len(outputs):
            msg = (
                f"Length of Inputs: {len(inputs)} and "
                f"Length of Outputs: {len(outputs)} must be equal."
            )
            config.LOGGER.error(msg)
            raise ValueError(msg)

    if indices is None:
        indices = jnp.asarray(
            index_shuffle(len(inputs), portion=portion),
            dtype=int,
        )
    elif not isinstance(indices, Array):
        if not isinstance(indices, Sequence):
            msg = f"'indices' must be a Sequence. Got {type(indices).__name__}"
            config.LOGGER.error(msg)
            raise TypeError(msg)
        indices = jnp.asarray(indices, dtype=int)

    indices = jnp.sort(indices)

    n_full = int(inputs.shape[0])

    used = jnp.zeros(n_full, dtype=bool)
    used = used.at[indices].set(True)
    validation_indices = jnp.sort(jnp.where(~used)[0])

    config.LOGGER.debug(f"{indices=}")

    self.validation_inputs = None
    self.validation_outputs = None
    self.validation_indices = None
    self._full_inputs = None
    self._full_outputs = None

    if validation_indices.size > 0:
        if materialize_validation_from_portion:
            self.validation_inputs = inputs[validation_indices]
            if outputs is not None:
                self.validation_outputs = outputs[validation_indices]
        else:
            self.validation_indices = validation_indices
            self._full_inputs = inputs
            self._full_outputs = outputs

    self.inputs = inputs[indices]
    self.outputs = outputs[indices] if outputs is not None else None
    self.indices = indices
    self.file_indices = file_indices
    self.num_data = len(self.inputs)

    def clone(self, *, copy_split: bool = True) -> DataShape:
    """Return a new data shape that holds the same working rows.

    The clone is built from these rows with a fresh index range, so the original
    ``indices`` are not applied again. Validation rows are copied across. The train
    and test split is copied only when this shape has been split and ``copy_split``
    is true.

    Args:
        copy_split: Copy ``train_*``, ``test_*``, ``samples``, and ``n_points``.
            Default: ``True``.

    Returns:
        The new data shape.

    """
    config.LOGGER.debug("Cloned.")
    # Pass identity indices so `inputs`/`outputs` are already the working rows
    # (global `self.indices` are not valid row picks into the subset tensor).
    n = len(self.inputs)
    ds = DataShape(
        self.inputs,
        self.outputs,
        indices=jnp.arange(n, dtype=int),
        portion=1.0,
        materialize_validation_from_portion=True,
    )
    ds.validation_inputs = self.validation_inputs
    ds.validation_outputs = self.validation_outputs
    if self.validation_indices is not None:
        ds.validation_indices = self.validation_indices
        ds._full_inputs = self._full_inputs
        ds._full_outputs = self._full_outputs
    if copy_split and self.been_split:
        ds.train_indices = self.train_indices
        ds.test_indices = self.test_indices
        ds.train_inputs = self.train_inputs
        ds.test_inputs = self.test_inputs
        ds.train_outputs = self.train_outputs
        ds.test_outputs = self.test_outputs
        ds.samples = self.samples
        ds.n_points = self.n_points
        ds.been_split = True
    return ds

    """Plot one sample and, when outputs exist, the matching target.

    ``show_normals``, ``normal_scale``, ``fig``, ``ax``, and ``fig_size`` are
    accepted so this method can stand in for [`Shape.draw`][pinnjax.geometry.base.Shape.draw].
    The image plot builds its own figure and does not use them.

    ``input_channel`` and ``output_channel`` choose one leading channel, ``"rgb"``,
    or ``"all"``. ``"all"`` draws one panel per channel. ``None`` uses the array as
    stored. Panels are laid out in one row or one column.

    Args:
        data_index: Sample to draw. Default: ``0``.
        show_normals: Ignored. Default: ``False``.
        normal_scale: Ignored. Default: ``1``.
        fig: Ignored. Default: ``None``.
        ax: Ignored. Default: ``None``.
        fig_size: Ignored.
        show: Display the figure before returning it. Default: ``True``.
        input_channel: Channel of the input sample. Default: ``0``.
        output_channel: Channel of the output sample. Default: ``0``.
        cmap: Colormap for a single-channel image. Default: ``"grey"``.
        subplot_orientation: ``"horizontal"`` or ``"vertical"``. Default: ``"horizontal"``.
        show_title: Put the sample index and file name above the figure.
            Default: ``False``.
        show_captions: Title each panel. Default: ``True``.
        save: Write the figure to disk. Default: ``False``.
        save_location: Directory for the saved figure. Default: ``None``.
        save_name: File name. Default: ``"comparison.pdf"``.
        resort: Move channel axes before display. ``None`` moves a single leading
            channel only. Default: ``None``.

    Returns:
        The Matplotlib figure and its first axes.

    Raises:
        IndexError: If ``data_index`` is outside the working rows.
        ValueError: If a channel setting does not match the array shape.

    """
    del show_normals, normal_scale, fig, ax, fig_size
    if data_index < 0 or data_index >= len(self.inputs):
        raise IndexError(
            f"Index {data_index} out of range for dataset length {len(self.inputs)}",
        )
    return _draw_arrays(
        self.inputs,
        self.outputs,
        data_index=data_index,
        input_channel=input_channel,
        output_channel=output_channel,
        cmap=cmap,
        file_indices=self.file_indices,
        subplot_orientation=subplot_orientation,
        show_title=show_title,
        show_captions=show_captions,
        show=show,
        save=save,
        save_location=save_location,
        save_name=save_name,
        resort=resort,
    )

    @classmethod
def from_files(
    cls,
    path: Path | str,
    *,
    portion: float = 1.0,
    input_folder_name: str = "input",
    output_folder_name: str | None = "output",
    mat_key: str = "groundTruth",
    resort: bool = False,
) -> DataShape:
    """Build a data shape from paired files in two folders.

    ``path / input_folder_name`` must be a directory. ``path / output_folder_name``
    is required unless ``output_folder_name`` is ``None``, which loads inputs only.
    Files are paired in sorted order. A numeric file stem sorts before a
    non-numeric one. Accepted suffixes are ``.jpg``, ``.png``, ``.csv``, ``.mat``,
    and ``.npy``. A MATLAB file is read from ``mat[mat_key].Segmentation``.
    ``resort`` stores an image as channels-first.

    ``portion`` selects the files. The constructor then receives that subset with
    ``portion=1``, so the file sample is not drawn a second time.

    Args:
        path: Directory that contains the input folder and the optional output folder.
        portion: Fraction of file pairs to keep. Default: ``1``.
        input_folder_name: Name of the input folder. Default: ``"input"``.
        output_folder_name: Name of the output folder, or ``None`` for inputs only.
            Default: ``"output"``.
        mat_key: MATLAB struct name. Default: ``"groundTruth"``.
        resort: Store images as channels-first. Default: ``False``.

    Returns:
        A data shape whose rows are the selected files.

    Raises:
        NotADirectoryError: If an expected folder is missing.
        ValueError: If the two folders do not contain the same number of files, or a
            MATLAB file is missing ``mat_key``.
        TypeError: If a file suffix is not supported.

    """
    input_files, output_files, indices, file_indices = _load_data_files(
        path,
        input_folder_name=input_folder_name,
        output_folder_name=output_folder_name,
        portion=portion,
    )
    inputs, outputs = _files_to_jax_arrays(
        input_files,
        output_files,
        mat_key=mat_key,
        resort=resort,
    )

    # portion = 1.0 because it would've already been split.
    return cls(
        inputs,
        outputs,
        portion=1.0,
        indices=indices,
        file_indices=file_indices,
    )

    @classmethod
def from_table(
    cls,
    table: str | Path | pl.DataFrame,
    *,
    input_columns: str | int | Sequence[str] | Sequence[int],
    output_columns: str | int | Sequence[str] | Sequence[int] | None = None,
    portion: float = 1.0,
    drop_nulls: bool = True,
    materialize_validation_from_portion: bool = True,
) -> DataShape:
    """Build a data shape from a CSV file or a Polars frame.

    A column specification is one name, one index, or a sequence of one of those.
    Names and indices cannot be mixed. Output columns are optional. A one-column
    output is reshaped to ``(n, 1)``. Rows with nulls in the selected columns are
    dropped when ``drop_nulls`` is true.

    ``portion`` selects the rows before construction. The constructor then receives
    that subset with ``portion=1``.

    Args:
        table: CSV path or an existing frame. A path must end in ``.csv``.
        input_columns: Columns used as inputs.
        output_columns: Columns used as outputs. Default: no outputs.
        portion: Fraction of rows to keep. Default: ``1``.
        drop_nulls: Drop rows with a null in a selected column. Default: ``True``.
        materialize_validation_from_portion: Copy held-out rows during construction.
            Default: ``True``.

    Returns:
        A data shape with one row per table record.

    Raises:
        ValueError: If the path is not a CSV, a column list is empty, a name is
            missing, or an input column is also an output column.
        TypeError: If a specification mixes names and indices.
        IndexError: If a column index is outside the frame.

    """

    def _normalize_columns(
        spec: str | int | Sequence[str] | Sequence[int],
        available: Sequence[str],
        *,
        arg_name: str,
    ) -> list[str]:
        cols = list(available)

        if isinstance(spec, (str, int)):
            items = [spec]
        elif isinstance(spec, Sequence):
            if len(spec) == 0:
                raise ValueError(f"'{arg_name}' cannot be empty.")
            items = list(spec)
        else:
            raise TypeError(f"'{arg_name}' has invalid type: {type(spec).__name__}")

        has_str = any(isinstance(_x, str) for _x in items)
        has_int = any(isinstance(_x, int) for _x in items)
        if has_str and has_int:
            raise TypeError(f"'{arg_name}' cannot mix str and int in one sequence.")

        if has_str:
            out = [str(_x) for _x in items]
            missing = [c for c in out if c not in cols]
            if missing:
                raise ValueError(f"'{arg_name}' unknown columns: {missing}")
            return out

        out: list[str] = []
        for idx in items:
            if not isinstance(idx, int):
                raise TypeError(f"'{arg_name}' must contain only str or only int.")
            if idx < 0 or idx >= len(cols):
                raise IndexError(
                    f"'{arg_name}' index {idx} out of range [0, {len(cols) - 1}]",
                )
            out.append(cols[idx])
        return out

    if isinstance(table, pl.DataFrame):
        df = table
    else:
        path = Path(table)
        if path.suffix.lower() != ".csv":
            raise ValueError(f"Expected .csv, got {path.suffix}")
        df = pl.read_csv(path)

    in_cols = _normalize_columns(
        input_columns,
        df.columns,
        arg_name="input_columns",
    )
    out_cols = (
        _normalize_columns(output_columns, df.columns, arg_name="output_columns")
        if output_columns is not None
        else []
    )

    overlap = sorted(set(in_cols).intersection(out_cols))
    if overlap:
        raise ValueError(f"Input/output columns overlap: {overlap}")

    selected = in_cols + out_cols
    df = df.select(selected)
    if drop_nulls:
        df = df.drop_nulls(subset=selected)

    x = df.select(in_cols).to_numpy().astype(float)
    y = None
    if out_cols:
        y = df.select(out_cols).to_numpy().astype(float)
        if y.ndim == 1:
            y = y[:, None]

    indices = None
    if portion != 1.0:
        indices = jnp.asarray(
            index_shuffle(len(x), portion=portion),
            dtype=int,
        )

    return cls(
        jnp.asarray(x, dtype=config.get_dtype()),
        (jnp.asarray(y, dtype=config.get_dtype()) if y is not None else None),
        indices=indices,
        portion=1.0,
        materialize_validation_from_portion=materialize_validation_from_portion,
    )

    def loss(self, residuals: Array) -> Array:
    """Calculate the loss for all collocation points.

    Evaluation uses the bound [`pinnjax.Loss`][pinnjax.Loss].

    Args:
        residuals: Array of residual values for each collocation point.

    Returns:

    loss_function = self.loss_function
    if loss_function is None:

    self.loss_val = loss_function(residuals)
    return self.loss_val

    def materialize_validation_from_portion(self) -> None:
    """Copy deferred held-out rows into ``validation_inputs`` / ``validation_outputs``.

    Only applies when the shape was built with ``portion < 1.0`` and
    ``materialize_validation_from_portion=False``, so row indices were set aside
    at construction. Calling this again after validation is already filled is a
    no-op. If no rows were ever held out (e.g. ``portion=1.0``), there is nothing
    to copy; logs a warning and returns.
    """
    if self.validation_inputs is not None:
        return
    if self.validation_indices is None or self.validation_indices.size == 0:
        config.LOGGER.warning(
            "All DATA was used in training/testing. Use a portion less than 1.0.",
        )
        return
    assert self._full_inputs is not None
    self.validation_inputs = self._full_inputs[self.validation_indices]
    if self._full_outputs is not None:
        self.validation_outputs = self._full_outputs[self.validation_indices]
    self.validation_indices = None
    self._full_inputs = None
    self._full_outputs = None

    def residuals(self, ops: DifferentialOperators) -> Array:
    """Calculate the residual values for all collocation points.

    Evaluation uses the bound [`pinnjax.Residual`][pinnjax.Residual].

    Args:
        ops: A [`DifferentialOperators`][pinnjax.DifferentialOperators] object.


    Returns:
        residuals: Array of residual values for each collocation point.

    Raises:
        InputError: If no collocation points have been generated for this Shape.
        InputError: If no [`pinnjax.Residual`][pinnjax.Residual]
            has been bound to this Shape.

    """
    samples = self.samples
    if samples is None:
        msg = "There are no samples associated with this shape. Call .sample() first."
        config.LOGGER.error(msg)
        raise config.InputError(msg)
    residual_function = self.residual_function
    if residual_function is None:
        msg = (
            "There is no residual function associated with this shape. "
            "Call .set_residual() first."
        )
        config.LOGGER.error(msg)
        raise config.InputError(msg)
    return residual_function(samples, ops)

    sampling_values: float | Sequence[float | int] | None = None,
    *,
    overwrite: bool = False,
    descriptor_count: int = 32,
) -> tuple[Array, int]:
    """Store collocation points on this shape.

    ``sampling_values`` is one number. ``None`` uses ``1000``. A list is
    rejected here. [`ComplexShape.sample`][pinnjax.geometry.complex.ComplexShape.sample]
    accepts one number per child. When points are already stored and
    ``overwrite`` is false, those points are returned unchanged.

    ``descriptor_count`` is used by
    [`OperatorGeometry.sample`][pinnjax.geometry.operator.OperatorGeometry.sample] and ignored
    here.

    Args:
        method: Sampler that draws the points.
        sampling_values: One sampling size. ``None`` uses the Sampler default.
        overwrite: Replace points that were already stored.
        descriptor_count: Descriptor sample count for an operator geometry.

    Returns:
        samples: Collocation points stored on ``samples``.
        n_points: Number of those points.

    Raises:
        ValueError: If ``sampling_values`` is a sequence.

    """
    del descriptor_count
    if sampling_values is not None and not isinstance(sampling_values, (float, int)):
        msg = "A Shape takes one sampling value. Pass a list to ComplexShape.sample."
        config.LOGGER.error(msg)
        raise ValueError(msg)

    if not overwrite and self.samples is not None and self.n_points > 0:
        return self.samples, self.n_points

    self.samples = jnp.asarray(
        method(self, sampling_values),
        dtype=config.get_dtype(),
    )
    self.n_points = len(self.samples)

    return self.samples, self.n_points

    def test_train_split(
    self,
    split_percentage: float = 0.5,
    *,
    overwrite: bool = False,
    seed: int | None = None,  # default: config.get_seed() # 100
    mode: Literal["shuffle", "stratified", "stratified_kfold"] = "shuffle",
    stratified_assignment: Literal["random", "ordered"] = "random",
    consecutive_samples: int = 5,  # group size
    train_per_group: int | None = 3,
    # if None: derived from split_percentage
    stratify_on: Literal["outputs", "inputs"] = "outputs",
    output_column: int = 0,  # if outputs is (N, k), which column to sort by.
    # stratified_kfold: requires consecutive_samples == n_folds; in each full block,
    # position j (0..n_folds-1) is test for fold j; partial tail block -> train only
    n_folds: int = 5,
    fold: int = 0,
) -> None:
    """Split the working rows into train and test sets.

    A second call leaves the existing split in place and logs a warning.
    ``overwrite`` replaces it.

    ``"shuffle"`` draws a permutation and gives the first fraction to train. At
    least one row is kept for train. ``"stratified"`` sorts by one column, cuts
    that order into blocks of ``consecutive_samples``, and takes
    ``train_per_group`` rows from each block. ``None`` derives that count from
    ``split_percentage``. ``"random"`` shuffles inside the block. ``"ordered"``
    keeps the sorted order. A leftover block of one row goes to train.

    ``"stratified_kfold"`` uses the same sorted blocks. ``consecutive_samples``
    must equal ``n_folds``. Position ``fold`` in each full block is the test row,
    and the other positions are train. A short tail block goes to train.
    ``split_percentage`` is not used in this mode.

    ``samples`` and ``n_points`` are set from the training inputs.

    Args:
        split_percentage: Fraction of rows for training. Required in ``(0, 1)`` for
            ``"shuffle"`` and ``"stratified"``. Default: ``0.5``.
        overwrite: Replace an existing split. Default: ``False``.
        seed: Seed for the shuffle. ``None`` uses ``config.get_seed()``.
        mode: ``"shuffle"``, ``"stratified"``, or ``"stratified_kfold"``.
            Default: ``"shuffle"``.
        stratified_assignment: ``"random"`` or ``"ordered"`` inside each stratified
            block. Default: ``"random"``.
        consecutive_samples: Block length for the stratified modes. Default: ``5``.
        train_per_group: Training rows taken from each stratified block. ``None``
            uses ``split_percentage``. Default: ``3``.
        stratify_on: ``"outputs"`` or ``"inputs"``. Default: ``"outputs"``.
        output_column: Column used as the sort key. Default: ``0``.
        n_folds: Number of folds for ``"stratified_kfold"``. Default: ``5``.
        fold: Which position in each block is the test row. Default: ``0``.

    Raises:
        ValueError: If the fraction, mode, block size, fold, or sort column is not valid.

    """
    if self.been_split is not True or overwrite is True:
        if overwrite:
            msg = "This DataShape was previously split. Overwriting."
            config.LOGGER.warning(msg)
        if split_percentage <= 0 or (split_percentage >= 1 and mode != "stratified_kfold"):
            msg = (
                "`split_percentage` must be between 0 and 1 (non-exclusive)."
                f" Got {split_percentage}."
            )
            config.LOGGER.error(msg)
            raise ValueError(msg)

        if seed is None:
            seed = config.get_seed()

        if mode == "shuffle":
            indices = index_shuffle(self.num_data, seed=seed)
            split = max(int(self.num_data * split_percentage), 1)
            self.train_indices = jnp.asarray(sorted(indices[:split]), dtype=int)
            self.test_indices = jnp.asarray(sorted(indices[split:]), dtype=int)
        elif mode == "stratified_kfold":
            if n_folds < 2:
                msg = "'n_folds' must be >= 2 for stratified_kfold mode."
                config.LOGGER.error(msg)
                raise ValueError(msg)
            if fold < 0 or fold >= n_folds:
                msg = f"'fold' must be in [0, n_folds). Got fold={fold}, n_folds={n_folds}."
                config.LOGGER.error(msg)
                raise ValueError(msg)
            if consecutive_samples < 2:
                msg = "'consecutive_samples' must be >= 2 for stratified_kfold mode."
                config.LOGGER.error(msg)
                raise ValueError(msg)
            if consecutive_samples != n_folds:
                msg = (
                    "'stratified_kfold' requires `consecutive_samples` == `n_folds` "
                    "so each ascending-life block assigns one sample per fold."
                )
                config.LOGGER.error(msg)
                raise ValueError(msg)
            sorted_idx = self._stratify_sort_indices(stratify_on, output_column)
            train_idx: list[int] = []
            test_idx: list[int] = []
            for start in range(0, len(sorted_idx), consecutive_samples):
                block = sorted_idx[start : start + consecutive_samples]
                if len(block) < consecutive_samples:
                    train_idx.extend(block)
                    continue
                for j, idx in enumerate(block):
                    if j == fold:
                        test_idx.append(idx)
                    else:
                        train_idx.append(idx)
            self.train_indices = jnp.asarray(sorted(train_idx), dtype=int)
            self.test_indices = jnp.asarray(sorted(test_idx), dtype=int)
        elif mode == "stratified":
            if stratified_assignment not in ("random", "ordered"):
                msg = (
                    "`stratified_assignment` must be 'random' or 'ordered'. "
                    f"Got {stratified_assignment!r}."
                )
                config.LOGGER.error(msg)
                raise ValueError(msg)
            if consecutive_samples < 2:
                msg = "`consecutive_samples` must be >= 2 for stratified mode."
                config.LOGGER.error(msg)
                raise ValueError(msg)
            sorted_idx = self._stratify_sort_indices(stratify_on, output_column)
            if train_per_group is None:
                tpg: int = round(consecutive_samples * split_percentage)
            else:
                tpg = int(train_per_group)
            tpg = max(1, min(tpg, consecutive_samples - 1))
            train_idx = []
            test_idx = []
            for start in range(0, len(sorted_idx), consecutive_samples):
                block = sorted_idx[start : start + consecutive_samples]
                if len(block) == 1:
                    train_idx.extend(block)
                    continue
                if stratified_assignment == "random":
                    random.Random(seed).shuffle(block)
                k = min(max(1, tpg), len(block) - 1)
                train_idx.extend(block[:k])
                test_idx.extend(block[k:])
            self.train_indices = jnp.asarray(sorted(train_idx), dtype=int)
            self.test_indices = jnp.asarray(sorted(test_idx), dtype=int)
        else:
            msg = (
                f"Invalid split mode: {mode}. "
                "Use 'shuffle', 'stratified', or 'stratified_kfold'."
            )
            config.LOGGER.error(msg)
            raise ValueError(msg)
        self.train_inputs, self.test_inputs = (
            self.inputs[self.train_indices],
            self.inputs[self.test_indices],
        )
        if self.outputs is None:
            self.train_outputs = None
            self.test_outputs = None
        else:
            self.train_outputs, self.test_outputs = (
                self.outputs[self.train_indices],
                self.outputs[self.test_indices],
            )
        self.samples = self.train_inputs
        self.n_points = len(self.train_inputs)
        self.been_split = True
    else:
        msg = (
            "This DataShape has already been split into test/train. "
            "Continuing without making changes"
        )
        config.LOGGER.warning(msg)

    class DataGeometry(ComplexShape, ABC):
    """A [`ComplexShape`][pinnjax.ComplexShape] whose only child is a [`DataShape`][pinnjax.DataShape].

    Training, evaluation, and the train or test split go through that child.
    ``evaluation`` is empty until ``assign_evaluation()``.

    Attributes:
        data_shape: The child dataset.
        evaluation: Evaluator bound to the test rows, or ``None``.

    """

    data_shape: DataShape
    evaluation: Evaluation | None

    def __init__(
        self,
        inputs: Array,
        outputs: Array | None = None,
        *,
        indices: Array | Sequence[int] | None = None,
        portion: float = 1.0,
        materialize_validation_from_portion: bool = True,
    ) -> None:
        """Wrap one data shape around these rows.

        Args:
            inputs: One row or sample per leading axis.
            outputs: Targets aligned with ``inputs``. Omit them for input-only data.
            indices: Positions to keep. Default: a shuffled fraction of the rows.
            portion: Fraction of rows to keep when ``indices`` is omitted. Default: ``1``.
            materialize_validation_from_portion: Copy held-out rows during construction.
                Default: ``True``.

        """
        data_shape = DataShape(
            inputs,
            outputs,
            indices=indices,
            portion=portion,
            materialize_validation_from_portion=materialize_validation_from_portion,
        )
        super().__init__([data_shape])
        self.data_shape = data_shape
        self.evaluation = None

    @classmethod
    def _from_data_shape(cls, data_shape: DataShape) -> Self:
        self = object.__new__(cls)
        ComplexShape.__init__(self, [data_shape])
        self.data_shape = data_shape
        self.evaluation = None
        return self

    def duplicate_data_shape(
        self,
        times: int = 1,
        *,
        copy_split: bool = True,
    ) -> list[DataShape]:
        """Append clones of the child data shape.

        Each clone is produced by [`DataShape.clone`][pinnjax.geometry.data.DataShape.clone] and
        added to ``shapes``. The original child stays in place.

        Args:
            times: How many clones to add. Default: ``1``.
            copy_split: Copy the train and test split onto each clone. Default: ``True``.

        Returns:
            The clones that were appended, not including the original child.

        Raises:
            ValueError: If ``times`` is less than 1.

        """
        if times < 1:
            raise ValueError(f"'times' must be >= 1, got {times}.")
        duplicates: list[DataShape] = []
        for _ in range(times):
            ds = self.data_shape.clone(copy_split=copy_split)
            self.shapes.append(ds)
            duplicates.append(ds)
        return duplicates

    @classmethod
    def from_files(
        cls,
        path: Path | str,
        *,
        input_folder_name: str = "input",
        output_folder_name: str | None = "output",
        portion: float = 1.0,
        mat_key: str = "groundTruth",
        resort: bool = False,
    ) -> Self:
        """Build a geometry from the same folder layout as [`DataShape.from_files`][pinnjax.geometry.data.DataShape.from_files].

        Args:
            path: Directory that contains the input folder and the optional output folder.
            input_folder_name: Name of the input folder. Default: ``"input"``.
            output_folder_name: Name of the output folder, or ``None`` for inputs only.
                Default: ``"output"``.
            portion: Fraction of file pairs to keep. Default: ``1``.
            mat_key: MATLAB struct name. Default: ``"groundTruth"``.
            resort: Store images as channels-first. Default: ``False``.

        Returns:
            A geometry whose child is the loaded data shape.

        Raises:
            NotADirectoryError: If an expected folder is missing.
            ValueError: If the two folders do not contain the same number of files, or a
                MATLAB file is missing ``mat_key``.
            TypeError: If a file suffix is not supported.

        """
        ds = DataShape.from_files(
            path,
            portion=portion,
            input_folder_name=input_folder_name,
            output_folder_name=output_folder_name,
            mat_key=mat_key,
            resort=resort,
        )
        return cls._from_data_shape(ds)

    @classmethod
    def from_table(
        cls,
        table: str | Path | pl.DataFrame,
        *,
        input_columns: str | int | Sequence[str] | Sequence[int],
        output_columns: str | int | Sequence[str] | Sequence[int] | None = None,
        portion: float = 1.0,
        drop_nulls: bool = True,
        materialize_validation_from_portion: bool = True,
    ) -> Self:
        """Build a geometry from the same table rules as [`DataShape.from_table`][pinnjax.geometry.data.DataShape.from_table].

        Args:
            table: CSV path or an existing frame. A path must end in ``.csv``.
            input_columns: Columns used as inputs.
            output_columns: Columns used as outputs. Default: no outputs.
            portion: Fraction of rows to keep. Default: ``1``.
            drop_nulls: Drop rows with a null in a selected column. Default: ``True``.
            materialize_validation_from_portion: Copy held-out rows during construction.
                Default: ``True``.

        Returns:
            A geometry whose child is the loaded data shape.

        Raises:
            ValueError: If the path is not a CSV, a column list is empty, a name is
                missing, or an input column is also an output column.
            TypeError: If a specification mixes names and indices.
            IndexError: If a column index is outside the frame.

        """
        ds = DataShape.from_table(
            table,
            input_columns=input_columns,
            output_columns=output_columns,
            portion=portion,
            drop_nulls=drop_nulls,
            materialize_validation_from_portion=materialize_validation_from_portion,
        )
        return cls._from_data_shape(ds)

    def validate(
        self,
        model: NeuralNetwork,
        evaluation: Evaluation | None = None,
    ) -> dict[str, float]:
        """Compute metrics on the rows held out by ``portion``.

        Deferred validation rows are copied first. If nothing was held out, this logs
        a warning and returns an empty dictionary. ``materialize_validation_from_portion()``
        cannot create those rows after construction.

        ``evaluation=None`` builds a [`TabularPointwiseEvaluation`][pinnjax.TabularPointwiseEvaluation]
        and binds the held-out rows. A passed evaluator is shallow-copied, then its
        ``inputs`` and ``truth`` are set to those rows, so the original object is unchanged.

        Args:
            model: Network to evaluate.
            evaluation: Evaluator to copy, or ``None`` to build a tabular one.
                Default: ``None``.

        Returns:
            Metric name to float. Empty when no rows were held out.

        Raises:
            RuntimeError: If this geometry has no outputs, or the held-out outputs are missing.
            TypeError: If ``evaluation`` has no ``inputs`` and ``truth`` attributes.

        """
        ds = self.data_shape
        if ds.outputs is None:
            msg = "Validation requires output data, but outputs is None."
            config.LOGGER.error(msg)
            raise RuntimeError(msg)

        from pinnjax.loss import TabularPointwiseEvaluation

        validation_inputs = ds.validation_inputs
        validation_outputs = ds.validation_outputs
        if validation_inputs is None and (
            ds.validation_indices is not None and ds.validation_indices.size > 0
        ):
            ds.materialize_validation_from_portion()
            validation_inputs = ds.validation_inputs
            validation_outputs = ds.validation_outputs
        if validation_inputs is None or validation_inputs.shape[0] == 0:
            config.LOGGER.warning(
                "All DATA was used in training/testing. Use a portion less than 1.0. "
                "Returning empty metrics.",
            )
            return {}
        if validation_outputs is None:
            msg = "Validation outputs are not available."
            config.LOGGER.error(msg)
            raise RuntimeError(msg)

        if evaluation is None:
            tabular = TabularPointwiseEvaluation()
            tabular.bind_tabular_data(validation_inputs, validation_outputs)
        else:
            copied = copy.copy(evaluation)
            if not hasattr(copied, "inputs") or not hasattr(copied, "truth"):
                msg = (
                    "When passing evaluation, it must have .inputs and .truth so "
                    "validation rows can be bound (e.g. TabularPointwiseEvaluation or "
                    "a tabular Evaluation with the same attributes)."
                )
                config.LOGGER.error(msg)
                raise TypeError(msg)
            tabular = cast("TabularPointwiseEvaluation", copied)
            tabular.inputs = validation_inputs
            tabular.truth = validation_outputs
        metrics = tabular.evaluate(model)
        return {k: float(v) for k, v in metrics.items()}

    def assign_evaluation(
        self,
        evaluation: Evaluation | None = None,
        *,
        use_test_split: bool = True,
        **evaluation_kwargs,
    ) -> Evaluation:
        """Bind an evaluator to the rows used by ``train()``.

        The evaluator is stored on ``evaluation``. Pass that object as ``evaluation``
        to [`train`][pinnjax.train.train].

        ``evaluation=None`` builds a [`DataPointwiseEvaluation`][pinnjax.DataPointwiseEvaluation].
        ``**evaluation_kwargs`` are forwarded only in that case. A passed evaluator is
        shallow-copied. Either way, ``inputs`` and ``truth`` are set from the test
        split, or from the full working rows when ``use_test_split`` is false.

        Args:
            evaluation: Evaluator to copy, or ``None`` to build one. Default: ``None``.
            use_test_split: Bind ``test_inputs`` and ``test_outputs``. Default: ``True``.
            **evaluation_kwargs: Constructor arguments for the built evaluator.

        Returns:
            The evaluator stored on this geometry.

        Raises:
            RuntimeError: If outputs are missing, or the test split has not been created.
            TypeError: If the evaluator has no ``inputs`` and ``truth`` attributes.

        """
        ds = self.data_shape
        if ds.outputs is None:
            msg = "Evaluation requires output data, but outputs is None."
            config.LOGGER.error(msg)
            raise RuntimeError(msg)

        from pinnjax.loss import DataPointwiseEvaluation

        if use_test_split:
            if not ds.been_split:
                msg = "Call test_train_split() before assign_evaluation()."
                config.LOGGER.error(msg)
                raise RuntimeError(msg)
            inputs = ds.test_inputs
            outputs = ds.test_outputs
        else:
            inputs = ds.inputs
            outputs = ds.outputs

        if outputs is None:
            msg = "Evaluation outputs are not available."
            config.LOGGER.error(msg)
            raise RuntimeError(msg)

        if evaluation is None:
            bound = DataPointwiseEvaluation(**evaluation_kwargs)
        else:
            copied = copy.copy(evaluation)
            if not hasattr(copied, "inputs") or not hasattr(copied, "truth"):
                msg = "evaluation must have .inputs and .truth (e.g. DataPointwiseEvaluation)."
                config.LOGGER.error(msg)
                raise TypeError(msg)
            bound = cast("DataPointwiseEvaluation", copied)

        bound.inputs = inputs
        bound.truth = outputs
        self.evaluation = bound
        return bound

    def evaluate(
        self,
        model: NeuralNetwork,
        evaluation: Evaluation | None = None,
        *,
        use_test_split: bool = True,
    ) -> dict[str, float]:
        """Compute test-split metrics for a trained network.

        These metrics are a check on held-out rows. They are not the training loss.
        ``evaluation=None`` uses ``self.evaluation`` when that has been assigned, and
        otherwise builds a [`DataPointwiseEvaluation`][pinnjax.DataPointwiseEvaluation].
        The evaluator is shallow-copied before the rows are bound.

        Args:
            model: Trained network.
            evaluation: Evaluator to use. Default: ``None``.
            use_test_split: Use ``test_inputs`` and ``test_outputs``. ``False`` uses the
                full working rows. Default: ``True``.

        Returns:
            Metric name to float, for example ``{"MSE": ..., "R2": ...}``.

        Raises:
            RuntimeError: If outputs are missing, no evaluator could be assigned, or the
                test split has not been created.
            TypeError: If the evaluator cannot bind inputs and targets.

        """
        ds = self.data_shape
        if ds.outputs is None:
            msg = "Evaluation requires output data, but outputs is None."
            config.LOGGER.error(msg)
            raise RuntimeError(msg)

        from pinnjax.loss import DataPointwiseEvaluation

        if evaluation is None:
            evaluation = self.evaluation
        if evaluation is None:
            self.assign_evaluation(
                DataPointwiseEvaluation(),
                use_test_split=use_test_split,
            )
            evaluation = self.evaluation
        if evaluation is None:
            msg = "Evaluation was not assigned."
            config.LOGGER.error(msg)
            raise RuntimeError(msg)
        if use_test_split:
            if not ds.been_split:
                msg = "Call test_train_split() before evaluate()."
                config.LOGGER.error(msg)
                raise RuntimeError(msg)
            inputs = ds.test_inputs
            outputs = ds.test_outputs
        else:
            inputs = ds.inputs
            outputs = ds.outputs
        if outputs is None:
            msg = "Evaluation requires output data, but outputs is None."
            config.LOGGER.error(msg)
            raise RuntimeError(msg)
        copied = copy.copy(evaluation)
        bind = getattr(copied, "bind_tabular_data", None)
        if bind is not None:
            cast("Callable[[Array, Array], None]", bind)(inputs, outputs)
            ev = cast("DataPointwiseEvaluation", copied)
        elif hasattr(copied, "inputs") and hasattr(copied, "truth"):
            ev = cast("DataPointwiseEvaluation", copied)
            ev.inputs = inputs
            ev.truth = outputs
        else:
            msg = "evaluation must support binding inputs and truth."
            config.LOGGER.error(msg)
            raise TypeError(msg)
        metrics = ev.evaluate(model)
        return {k: float(v) for k, v in metrics.items()}

    def predict(
        self,
        model: NeuralNetwork,
        *,
        use_test_split: bool = False,
    ) -> Array:
        """Predict outputs without requiring ground-truth output data.

        This is the input-only counterpart to [`evaluate`][pinnjax.geometry.data.DataGeometry.evaluate].
        It performs inference only and therefore works when ``outputs`` is ``None``.

        Args:
            model: Trained [`NeuralNetwork`][pinnjax.NeuralNetwork].
            use_test_split: If ``True``, predict only on ``test_inputs`` and require
                [`test_train_split`][pinnjax.geometry.data.DataGeometry.test_train_split] to have
                been called. If ``False``, predict on the complete working input pool.

        Returns:
            Batched model predictions corresponding to the selected inputs.

        """
        ds = self.data_shape

        if use_test_split:
            if not ds.been_split:
                msg = "Call test_train_split() before predicting on the test split."
                config.LOGGER.error(msg)
                raise RuntimeError(msg)
            inputs = ds.test_inputs
        else:
            inputs = ds.inputs

        return jax.vmap(model)(inputs)

    # Convenience properties - delegate to data_shape
    @property
    def inputs(self):
        """Return the child data shape's input rows."""
        return self.data_shape.inputs

    @property
    def outputs(self) -> Array | None:
        """Return the child data shape's output rows."""
        return self.data_shape.outputs

    @property
    def indices(self):
        """Return the row indices kept in the working set."""
        return self.data_shape.indices

    @property
    def num_data(self):
        """Return the cached input and output shapes from the child data shape."""
        return self.data_shape.num_data

    @property
    def shape(self):
        """Return the cached input and output shapes from the child data shape."""
        return self.data_shape.shape

    @property
    def been_split(self):
        """Return whether the child data shape has been split."""
        return self.data_shape.been_split

    @property
    def validation_inputs(self) -> Array | None:
        """Return held-out input rows, if they have been materialized."""
        return self.data_shape.validation_inputs

    @property
    def validation_outputs(self) -> Array | None:
        """Return held-out output rows, if they have been materialized."""
        return self.data_shape.validation_outputs

    def materialize_validation_from_portion(self) -> None:
        """See [`DataShape.materialize_validation_from_portion`][pinnjax.geometry.data.DataShape.materialize_validation_from_portion]."""
        self.data_shape.materialize_validation_from_portion()

    def test_train_split(
        self,
        split_percentage: float = 0.5,
        *,
        overwrite: bool = False,
        seed: int | None = None,  # default: config.get_seed() # 100
        mode: Literal["shuffle", "stratified", "stratified_kfold"] = "shuffle",
        stratified_assignment: Literal["random", "ordered"] = "random",
        consecutive_samples: int = 5,  # group size
        train_per_group: int | None = 3,
        # if None: derived from split_percentage
        stratify_on: Literal["outputs", "inputs"] = "outputs",
        output_column: int = 0,  # if outputs is (N, k), which column to sort by
        n_folds: int = 5,
        fold: int = 0,
    ) -> None:
        """Split the child data shape with these same arguments.

        See [`DataShape.test_train_split`][pinnjax.geometry.data.DataShape.test_train_split].
        """
        self.data_shape.test_train_split(
            split_percentage=split_percentage,
            overwrite=overwrite,
            seed=seed,
            mode=mode,
            stratified_assignment=stratified_assignment,
            consecutive_samples=consecutive_samples,
            train_per_group=train_per_group,
            stratify_on=stratify_on,
            output_column=output_column,
            n_folds=n_folds,
            fold=fold,
        )
